description: Learn how to build engaging, responsive, and interactive web interfaces from scratch.

courses.title: Web Foundations: From Zero to Your First Line of Code
courses.description: Learn complete HTML structure and CSS styling from the basics through positioning & float techniques. This course serves as the foundation before moving on to modern Flexbox and Grid layouts.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main function of HTML when building a web page?
options: Connecting the browser to a DNS server
Defining the skeleton and content structure of the page
Styling colors, typography, and page layout
Running interactive logic and animations in the browser
quizQuestions.explanation: HTML is responsible for building the skeleton and structure of a web page (what content is on the page), while visual appearance is handled by CSS and interactivity by JavaScript.

quizQuestions.question: How does a browser treat plain text without HTML markup elements?
options: The browser refuses to display the page and returns a 404 error
The browser automatically adds an <h1> tag to the first sentence
The browser automatically applies heading formatting and paragraph spacing
The browser ignores extra spaces and blank lines, merging the text into a single continuous flow
quizQuestions.explanation: Browsers read HTML using whitespace collapsing rules: extra spaces and line breaks are ignored, and text is merged into a single continuous line/flow unless marked up with elements.

quizQuestions.question: Why does a website typically have a file named index.html in its root folder?
options: Because browsers refuse to process HTML if the file is not named index
Because browsers require the main file to have the smallest possible size
Because the server automatically loads index.html when the domain is visited
Because web protocols restrict public access to only this single file
quizQuestions.explanation: By web server convention, when a URL does not specify a particular filename (for example https://contoh.com), the server looks for and serves index.html by default.

quizQuestions.question: Which nested HTML element syntax follows the correct rules?
quizQuestions.explanation:
The element opened last must be closed first (LIFO). In this case, is opened after

, so must be closed before

.

quizQuestions.question: Where must HTML attributes be written and what is their basic format?
options: Between the opening tag and closing tag using the format (name, value)
In either the opening or closing tag using the format [name=value]
In the opening tag only using the format name="value"
In the closing tag using the format name: value;
quizQuestions.explanation: Attributes are always placed inside the opening tag, separated by a space after the tag name, using the syntax name="value".

quizQuestions.question: What is the fundamental difference between the id and class attributes in an HTML document?
options: class must have a unique value per page, while the id attribute may be duplicated
id is written in the closing tag, while class must be written in the opening tag
id is only used for scripts, while class is only for color styling
id must be unique per element, while class can be shared across multiple elements
quizQuestions.explanation: The id attribute is a unique identifier (only one element per id in a document), whereas class is a group marker that can be assigned to many elements.

quizQuestions.question: Why must the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration be placed on the very first line of an HTML document?
options: So the browser applies modern HTML standards and prevents quirks mode
So all text in the document is automatically rendered in a large size
To load the basic JavaScript function library into the browser page
To enable an internet network connection for all document content
quizQuestions.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> instructs the browser to render the page using modern HTML standards (standards mode) and avoid legacy quirks mode.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main purpose of the <head> element in an HTML document?
options: Displaying the largest article title centered on the page automatically
Storing document metadata that is not displayed directly in the web page body
Displaying the logo and main navigation bar at the top of the browser screen
Holding all article text, interactive forms, and content images
quizQuestions.explanation: The <head> element is a container for document metadata (tab <title>, charset, CSS links, scripts) and its contents are not rendered as visual page content.

quizQuestions.question: The hierarchical tree structure of HTML elements stored in the browser's memory when reading a document is called...
quizQuestions.explanation: The DOM (Document Object Model) Tree represents the nested parent, child, and sibling relationships of all elements in a web document.

quizQuestions.question: Consider the URL https://contoh.com/artikel/belajar-html. The protocol and domain name components are respectively...
quizQuestions.explanation: URL components: the protocol is 'https', the domain name is 'contoh.com', and the path is '/artikel/belajar-html'.

quizQuestions.question: Which element is appropriate for a step-by-step list of instructions where order matters?
quizQuestions.explanation: An ordered list (<ol>) is used when the sequence of items matters, displayed with automatic numbering.

quizQuestions.question: The required attribute on that specifies the image source is...
quizQuestions.explanation: src specifies the image source. alt is alternative text, not the image source itself.

quizQuestions.question: Which element is used for a long quotation that stands alone as a block?
quizQuestions.explanation: blockquote is used for long block-level quotations, unlike q which is inline for short quotations.

quizQuestions.question: How many <main> elements are allowed in a single HTML page?
options: Must equal the number of sections
quizQuestions.explanation: There may only be one <main> per page, because it represents the single primary content of that page.

quizQuestions.question: Why is <div class="header"> considered worse practice than <header>?
options: Browsers and search engines have difficulty recognizing its semantic role
div elements are forbidden from having styling classes under the HTML5 specification
div is only designed to wrap short inline text fragments
header uses built-in compression so it renders much faster
quizQuestions.explanation: div is a generic element with no semantic meaning, whereas header explicitly states its own role.

quizQuestions.question: The three basic elements that make up an HTML table are...
options: table, tr, and td or th
quizQuestions.explanation: table acts as the container, tr represents a row, and td/th represent data or header cells inside that row.

quizQuestions.question: Which attribute makes a single table cell span across multiple columns at once?
quizQuestions.explanation: colspan stretches a cell horizontally, spanning across multiple columns at once.

quizQuestions.question: What happens if an <input> inside a form is not given a name attribute?
options: Data from that input is not sent when the form is submitted
The data is still sent with an automatic name
quizQuestions.explanation: name is the key paired with the value when data is submitted. Without name, that data is not included in the submission.

quizQuestions.question: The main difference between the GET and POST methods on a form element is...
options: GET cannot be used to send data at all
POST is only for search forms
GET places data in the URL, while POST places data in the request body
quizQuestions.explanation: GET appends data as parameters in the URL, whereas POST places data in the request body so it is not visible in the URL.

quizQuestions.question: Which character reference is correct for the '<' sign so it is not parsed as the start of a tag?
quizQuestions.explanation: < is the named entity for the < sign. > is for the > sign, not for <.

questionPool.question: What is the main function of a network switch in a network?
options: Connecting multiple computers and forwarding data to the right target
Translating website domain names into the sender's destination IP address
Displaying the visual web page interface directly on the user's monitor
Securely storing website database files and multimedia assets
questionPool.explanation: A switch acts as a central point that connects multiple devices, so you don't have to run separate cables to every computer.

questionPool.question: The term "internet" most accurately describes...
options: The largest website in the world
A single giant computer that stores all websites
A network of many interconnected networks
A program for opening web pages
questionPool.explanation: Internet comes from the idea of an interconnected network: smaller networks connected together into one global network.

questionPool.question: A company that operates routers and connects your home network to networks around the world is called...
questionPool.explanation: An ISP manages routers that connect with other ISPs' routers, allowing data to reach different parts of the world.

questionPool.question: Which statement best describes the difference between a website and a web page?
options: A web page is a single page, whereas a website is a collection of interconnected web pages
A website can only be opened through an app, whereas a web page is opened through a browser
They are the exact same thing and only differ in spelling
A web page always contains videos, whereas a website only contains text
questionPool.explanation: A web page is like a single sheet of paper, while a website is the "book"—a collection of pages linked together.

questionPool.question: What connects one web page to another web page within a website?
questionPool.explanation: A hyperlink lets you navigate between pages, whether within the same domain or across different domains.

questionPool.question: Who is the British scientist who proposed the idea of the World Wide Web while working at CERN?
questionPool.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the WWW in 1989 to make it easier for scientists to share information.

questionPool.question: Which statement is true about the relationship between the internet and the web?
options: The web is one of the services that runs on top of the internet infrastructure
The internet can only be used to open websites
The web is the network infrastructure, while the internet is one of its websites
The internet and the web are two names for the same thing
questionPool.explanation: The internet is like a highway, and the web is one of the "vehicles" traveling on it. Other services like email and online games also use the internet.

questionPool.question: In the request-response cycle, the party that sends a request to the server is called...
questionPool.explanation: The browser acts as the client because it is the one requesting data, while the server responds to it.

questionPool.question: Which statement is true about a web server?
options: It can refer to both the computer (hardware) and the software that serves requests over HTTP
It is simply a cable that connects the browser to the internet
It is always a huge, ultra-high-performance computer
It is only a program that runs on the user's mobile phone
questionPool.explanation: A web server encompasses both the hardware side (the computer) and the software side (the program receiving requests) working together.

questionPool.question: Which of the following is an example of web server software?
questionPool.explanation: NGINX and Apache are examples of web servers. Firefox is a browser.

questionPool.question: What is the main job of a DNS server?
options: Displaying web pages on the user's screen
Providing the IP address that corresponds to a domain name
Storing a website's HTML and CSS files
Encrypting all data sent by the browser
questionPool.explanation: DNS is like the phone book of the internet: it translates easy-to-remember domain names into IP addresses that computers use.

questionPool.question: Before asking a DNS server, the browser first checks...
options: The contents of the website's JavaScript configuration file
The local DNS cache containing records of previous IP addresses
The remaining storage capacity of the server's hard drive
A list of all internet service providers in the world
questionPool.explanation: If the IP address is already in the DNS cache, the browser doesn't need to ask the DNS server, making the process faster.

questionPool.question: Why do we use domain names even though computers access websites via IP addresses?
options: Because domains are easy for humans to remember, while machines use IPs behind the scenes
Because the numeric IP address format is outdated and has been abandoned globally
Because domain names completely eliminate the server's need for an IP address
Because browsers process text domain names much faster than numbers
questionPool.explanation: Domain names are just for human convenience. Computers still use IP addresses, and DNS translates between the two.

questionPool.question: In the URL https://contoh.com/belajar/html, the contoh.com part is called the...
questionPool.explanation: Protocol = https, domain name = contoh.com, path = /belajar/html.

questionPool.question: The standard protocol used by browsers and web servers to exchange data is...
questionPool.explanation: HTTP is the data exchange protocol on the web. HTML is a markup language for page structure, so don't confuse the two.

questionPool.question: The browser receives a response with status code 404. What does this mean?
options: The server is experiencing an internal error
The user's internet connection was lost
The requested page or resource was not found
questionPool.explanation: 200 means success, 404 means not found, and 500 means the server encountered a problem.

questionPool.question: What is the role of HTML in a web page?
options: Connecting the browser with the DNS server
Defining the structure or skeleton of the page content
questionPool.explanation: HTML is the skeleton of the page. Colors and layout are handled by CSS, and interactivity is handled by JavaScript.

questionPool.question: To change text colors and spacing between elements, you use...
questionPool.explanation: CSS is responsible for styling and appearance: colors, font sizes, spacing, and layout.

questionPool.question: A button displays a message when clicked. Which technology plays the primary role in creating that interaction?
questionPool.explanation: JavaScript makes a page react to user actions, such as button clicks.

questionPool.question: A page appears with all its text and images, but without colors, spacing, or a neat layout. Which part likely failed to load?
questionPool.explanation: HTML has already provided the page content. A plain appearance like this indicates that CSS was not applied or failed to load.

questionPool.question: HTML stands for...
questionPool.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard language for structuring documents and web pages.

questionPool.question: Why is HTML categorized as a markup language rather than a programming language?
options: Because HTML structures content without branching computation logic
Because HTML is limited to designing data tables and form elements
Because HTML files do not require a compilation process before running
Because HTML code cannot be processed directly by modern browsers
questionPool.explanation: HTML is a markup language: it defines what is a heading, paragraph, image, or link, without having algorithmic logic or conditions like if/else.

questionPool.question: In a website-building analogy, the role of HTML is best compared to...
options: The frame and walls of a house
The paint and floor colors of a house
A security fence protecting the house
questionPool.explanation: HTML is the physical frame (structure), CSS is the aesthetic finish (paint/decoration), and JavaScript is interactivity (electricity).

questionPool.question: When you type text with many spaces and line breaks in an HTML file without markup tags, why does the browser merge them into one?
options: Because the browser applies whitespace collapsing rules
Because the HTML file hasn't been compressed with a size-reduction algorithm
Because the browser's parser engine fails to read space characters
Because browsers require every space to be written in hexadecimal format
questionPool.explanation: Browser rendering rules ignore extra spaces and line breaks in plain text; structure must be explicitly declared using HTML tags.

questionPool.question: In a website project folder, the main file that a server will automatically send by default is named...
questionPool.explanation: The standard web server convention is to serve 'index.html' automatically when the requested URL points to a main directory without specifying a filename.

questionPool.question: What is the difference between opening an HTML file with a 'file://' prefix compared to 'https://'?
options: file:// opens it directly from your device's local storage without an internet server
There is no difference; both always fetch files from a cloud server
https:// can only be opened if the computer does not have a browser
file:// requires a high-speed internet connection
questionPool.explanation: The 'file://' URI scheme reads files directly from the computer's local storage, whereas 'https://' requests files from a web server over the internet.

questionPool.question: The three parts that make up a complete HTML element are...
options: Domain name, protocol, and status code
Opening tag, content, and closing tag
questionPool.explanation:
An HTML element consists of an opening tag (e.g.,

), content (text or child elements), and a closing tag (e.g.,

).

questionPool.question: The key characteristic of a closing tag in HTML is...
options: Using an exclamation mark after the angle bracket (!p>)
Using a hyphen at the end of the element name (<p->)

Using a forward slash before the element name (

)
questionPool.explanation:
A closing tag is always marked with a forward slash '/' before the element name inside the angle brackets, such as

or .

questionPool.question: What happens if you forget to write a closing tag on an element?
options: The text across the entire document will automatically flip to right-to-left
The operating system automatically cancels reading all files in the folder
The browser guesses the element's boundary, so content wrapping may turn out wrong
The browser immediately shows a fatal error message and closes the page
questionPool.explanation: Browsers have built-in error tolerance, but their guesses often cause subsequent content to be formatted unintentionally.

questionPool.question: Which hierarchy of heading tags (h1-h6) is semantically correct?
options: Use <h1> as often as possible in every paragraph
The order of heading levels has no semantic meaning whatsoever
Use <h3> for the main title if you don't want the text to look too large
Use <h1> for the main page title, then <h2> for major subsections beneath it
questionPool.explanation: Headings reflect document hierarchy: <h1> is the main topic of the document, <h2> is a subtopic, and so on. Font size is controlled by CSS, not by arbitrarily changing heading levels.

questionPool.question: Which of the following elements is an empty/void element without a closing tag?
questionPool.explanation: (line break) and are examples of void elements in HTML that hold no text content inside them and therefore do not need a closing tag.

questionPool.question: Where is the correct place to write an HTML attribute?
options: Between the element's text content and the start of the document's closing tag
Inside the closing tag, placed right before the closing slash
Inside the opening tag, after the element name and separated by a space
Outside the angle brackets, right before the opening character of the element tag
questionPool.explanation: Attributes are always placed inside the opening tag after the tag name, separated by a space character.

questionPool.question:
Look at the following code:

Halo

. Which statement is TRUE?
options: Writing two attributes at once in a single tag is a syntax error
The id attribute may be reused repeatedly on other paragraph elements
The id attribute with the value 'pesan' must be unique within that document
The class attribute must have a unique value across the entire document
questionPool.explanation: The value of an id attribute must be unique within a single web page document, whereas a class name can be shared by many different elements.

questionPool.question: The alt attribute on an image element serves to...
options: Apply color filter effects to the photo
Store a backup image on another server
Automatically resize the height and width of the image
Provide alternative text for screen readers or when the image fails to load
questionPool.explanation: The alt (alternative text) attribute is essential for screen reader accessibility and serves as fallback text when an image fails to display.

questionPool.question: Which global attribute allows visitors to edit text directly in the browser?
questionPool.explanation: The global attribute contenteditable="true" makes an element's text content directly editable by the user in the browser.

questionPool.question: The <!DOCTYPE html> declaration is placed on...
options: The very first line of the entire HTML document file
The end of the document after the </html> tag
Inside the <body> tag at the very bottom
Inside the <head> tag after the <title> tag
questionPool.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> must be placed on the very first line at the top before the opening <html> tag so the browser renders in standards mode.

questionPool.question: Which element is the root element of the entire HTML document tree?
questionPool.explanation: The <html> element wraps all of the web page's contents and serves as the root node in the DOM tree.

questionPool.question: Which content belongs inside the <head> element?
options: The <meta charset="utf-8"> tag and the <title> tag
questionPool.explanation: The <head> element contains metadata instructions and the browser document title (<title>), not visual content rendered on the main screen.

questionPool.question: Which element holds all the visual content displayed in the user's browser window?
questionPool.explanation: All elements meant to be seen and interacted with by users (text, images, buttons, videos) must be placed inside the <body> tag.

questionPool.question: In the Document Object Model (DOM) tree concept, the relationship of the <head> and <body> elements to the <html> element is...
options: All three sit at the same hierarchy level without any parent-child relationship
<body> acts as the main parent of both the <head> and <html> elements
<head> and <body> are children of <html> and siblings to each other
<html> is a child element of <head>, while <body> is an outer element
questionPool.explanation: The <html> element is the parent, while <head> and <body> are direct child elements of <html> at the same level (siblings).

questionPool.question: Which element is appropriate for a step-by-step list of instructions where order matters?
questionPool.explanation: An ordered list (<ol>) is used for lists where order matters, displayed with automatic numbering.

questionPool.question: In a <dl> element, what is the function of <dt>?
options: Displays the term to be defined
questionPool.explanation: <dt> (description term) contains the term, while <dd> (description details) contains its explanation.

questionPool.question: You set width and height on with a ratio that does not match the original image. What happens?
options: The browser refuses to display the image
The image appears squished or stretched, out of proportion
questionPool.explanation: Setting both width and height at once with the wrong ratio makes the image appear out of proportion. It is best to set only one of them.

questionPool.question: Which element preserves spaces and line breaks exactly as written in the source code?
questionPool.explanation: <pre> displays its contents as-is, including extra spaces and line breaks that browsers normally ignore.

questionPool.question: The main difference between <blockquote> and <q> is...
options: Both are identical in appearance and semantics, differing only in element name
<q> is specifically for book title quotes, while <blockquote> is for spoken dialogue quotes
<blockquote> formats text in italics, while <q> formats text in bold
<blockquote> is for long block quotations, while <q> is for short inline quotations
questionPool.explanation: blockquote is a block-level element for standalone long quotations, whereas q is inline for short quotations within a sentence.

questionPool.question: The required attribute on an <a> element for a link to work is...
questionPool.explanation: href specifies the link destination. Without href, the a element does not point anywhere.

questionPool.question: Which element is used to mark words that need vocal stress emphasis, and is displayed in italics by default?
questionPool.explanation: em (emphasis) marks stress emphasis and is displayed in italics by default. strong marks importance and is displayed in bold.

questionPool.question: You want to link navigation to another section on the same page, with id="hobi" on the target element. How should href be written?
questionPool.explanation: A hash sign followed by the id name (for example: #hobi) tells the browser to jump to the element with that id on the same page.

questionPool.question: Which of the following correctly pairs an element with its function?
options: <mark> highlights text with a yellow background by default
<sup> displays smaller text below the baseline
<sub> displays larger text above the baseline
questionPool.explanation: mark highlights text, defaulting to a yellow background with black text. sub appears below the baseline and sup appears above the baseline, both in smaller text. br does not need a closing tag.

questionPool.question: Why is grouping content with just <div class="header"> considered 'semantically meaningless'?
options: Because browsers forbid using the header class name on a generic div element
Because browsers and screen readers cannot understand its meaning without reading the class name
Because div elements automatically trigger validation warnings in the HTML5 web standard
Because a div element may only be used at most once per file
questionPool.explanation: div is a generic element with no inherent meaning. Class names are only labels for humans, not structural role information understood by browsers or search engines.

questionPool.question: How many <main> elements are allowed on a single page?
options: As many as the number of sections
Must match the number of articles
questionPool.explanation: There can only be one main element on a page, because it represents the single primary content of that page.

questionPool.question: An <aside> is placed inside an <article>. What does that mean?
options: It contains info related to that article, but not part of its core content
It replaces the article header's function
It contains info related to the page as a whole
It serves as the main title of the article
questionPool.explanation: An aside inside an article contains supporting info for that article. Outside an article, an aside contains info related to the entire page.

questionPool.question: Which element should ideally begin with a heading as its first element?
questionPool.explanation: section is used to group thematically related content, and should ideally begin with a heading that serves as the title for that section.

questionPool.question: When should you use <div> instead of semantic elements like <article> or <section>?
options: Only for text in the middle of a sentence
Always, div is safer to use anywhere
When no semantic element matches the meaning of that content
div should never be used anymore since HTML5
questionPool.explanation: div is used when no semantic element fits, purely for grouping or styling purposes.

questionPool.question: The difference between <div> and <span> is...
options: div is inline, span is block
span can only be used inside a table
div is block-level, span is inline
questionPool.explanation: div is a block-level generic container, while span is its inline version, used for a small portion of text within a sentence.

questionPool.question: The three basic building-block elements of an HTML table are...
options: table, tr, and td or th
questionPool.explanation: table acts as the wrapper, tr for rows, and td or th for the cells inside those rows.

questionPool.question: Which attribute makes a single table cell span across multiple columns at once?
questionPool.explanation: colspan stretches a cell horizontally (spanning multiple columns). rowspan stretches it vertically.

questionPool.question: Which table element serves as the title for the entire table?
questionPool.explanation: caption is the title for the entire table, written right after the opening table tag.

questionPool.question: Which input type hides typed characters as asterisks by default?
questionPool.explanation: type="password" displays each character as an asterisk or dot, hiding the input from view on screen.

questionPool.question: What happens if an <input> is not given a name attribute when a form is submitted?
options: The form fails completely and cannot be submitted
The browser will add a random name
The data from that input is not submitted
The data is still submitted with an automatic name
questionPool.explanation: name is the key paired with the value when data is sent. Without name, that input's data is not included in the submission.

questionPool.question: Which element is used for multi-line long text input, such as a comment box?
questionPool.explanation: textarea is specifically designed for multi-line long text, unlike input which is always a single line.

questionPool.question: How do you associate a <label> with its corresponding input?
options: Setting a name attribute with the same value on both the label and the input
Relying on the browser to automatically link it to the nearest input
Placing the label element right above the input without additional attributes
Giving the input an id and the label a for attribute with identical values
questionPool.explanation: The for attribute on label must have the exact same value as the id on the target input.

questionPool.question: The main difference between the GET and POST methods on a form is...
options: GET puts data in the URL, while POST puts data in the request body
POST is slower because the data is larger
Both are identical, there is no difference
GET is only for login forms
questionPool.explanation: GET includes data as parameters in the URL, whereas POST places data in the request body so it is not visible in the URL.

questionPool.question: Why can't the '<' sign be written directly as part of HTML text content?
options: Because that sign is not on the keyboard
Because it may only be used inside attributes
Because the browser will mistake it for the start of a tag
Because lowercase letters are forbidden in HTML
questionPool.explanation: The < sign has a special meaning as the start of a tag in HTML, so to display it as plain text you need a character reference such as <.

questionPool.question: Which is the correct character reference for the copyright symbol (©)?
questionPool.explanation: © is the named entity for the copyright symbol. Alternatively, the numeric entity © produces the same display.

questionPool.question: Why is CSS called a declarative language rather than a programming language?
options: Because CSS requires a database to store styling rules
Because CSS only runs on the server side without browser interaction
Because CSS must be compiled first before it can be read by the browser
Because CSS only declares the desired appearance without having logic such as branching or loops
questionPool.explanation: CSS is declarative because developers simply declare the desired visual properties (for example, color or size), and the browser executes them without needing programming logic like if-else or loops.

questionPool.question: What does the acronym CSS officially stand for?
questionPool.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheet, the official web standard for controlling the presentation and appearance of HTML documents.

questionPool.question: One of the main advantages of separating styling using CSS compared to setting appearance directly in the HTML structure is...
options: CSS eliminates the need for HTML tags in a document
A CSS file can completely replace a web server's function
CSS automatically gives a website login and authentication features
A single CSS file can be shared across many HTML pages at once
questionPool.explanation: With external CSS, a single stylesheet file can be linked to multiple HTML pages, so styling changes only need to be made in one place without editing every page again.

questionPool.question: A CSS rule consists of two main parts, namely...
questionPool.explanation: The basic structure of a CSS rule always starts with a selector (the target HTML element) followed by a declaration block inside curly braces { }.

questionPool.question: Among the following CSS declarations, which one is considered INVALID by the browser?
questionPool.explanation: In CSS length values, there must be no space between the number and its unit. Writing 'margin: 2 em;' is invalid and will be ignored by the browser; the correct form is 'margin: 2em;'.

questionPool.question: What is the correct syntax for writing a comment inside a CSS file?
questionPool.explanation: Comments in CSS are written using the /* ... */ format. The <!-- ... --> format is an HTML comment, while // and # are not official comment syntax in standard CSS.

questionPool.question: What is the most appropriate way to attach an External Style Sheet to an HTML document?
options: Using a <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> tag inside the <head> tag
Using a <meta css="style.css"> tag in the <html> tag
Using a <script src="style.css"> tag at the end of the <body> tag
Using a <style href="style.css"> tag inside the <footer> tag
questionPool.explanation: An External Style Sheet is linked using a <link rel="stylesheet" href="..."> element placed in the <head> section of the HTML document.

questionPool.question: The main characteristic of an Embedded (Internal) Style Sheet is...
options: It can be used automatically by the entire website without needing to be linked
CSS rules are written inside a <style> tag and apply only to that single HTML document
CSS rules are written in a separate .js file
Styling is applied directly on an element attribute without using a selector
questionPool.explanation: An Embedded Style Sheet is placed inside a <style> tag (usually inside <head>) and its scope is limited only to the HTML file where that tag is located.

questionPool.question: Why is using Inline Styles (<tag style='...'>) generally NOT recommended for large-scale projects?
options: Because inline styles can only display black and white colors
Because inline styles automatically disable all hyperlinks on the page
Because modern browsers no longer support the style attribute
Because it mixes content structure with presentation styling, making it hard to maintain and impossible to reuse
questionPool.explanation: Inline styles attach styling directly to individual tags, mixing HTML and CSS together and making code maintenance very complicated when uniform design changes are needed.
A group selector allows combining multiple selectors using commas so that the same declaration block can be applied to all of those elements concisely.

questionPool.question: You have written CSS code properly in the style.css file, but when opening index.html in the browser, the appearance is still plain with no styling. What is the most common possible cause of this issue?
options: Not including a <canvas> graphic element inside the document structure
The HTML file does not yet contain an <h1> heading element inside the page body
Not including a <link rel="stylesheet"> tag in the <head> section of the HTML file
The web browser has not enabled JavaScript language processing support
questionPool.explanation: An external CSS file will not be applied to an HTML page unless it is explicitly linked using a <link rel="stylesheet" href="..."> tag inside <head>.

questionPool.question: Which CSS property is used to set the background color of an element like <footer>?
questionPool.explanation: The 'background-color' property sets an element's background color, whereas 'color' is used for text color.

questionPool.question: How does the concept of inheritance work in CSS?
options: All CSS selectors automatically inherit JavaScript functions
Some styling properties from a parent element are automatically passed down to elements inside it
A child HTML file automatically copies all HTML code from its parent
Browsers automatically remove styling from outer elements
questionPool.explanation: Inheritance in CSS means child elements inherit the values of certain properties (such as color and font-family) from their wrapping parent element.

questionPool.question:
If there are two rules for the same element (for example 'p { color: blue; }' followed on the next line by 'p { color: green; }'), what color will appear on the

text, and why?
options: Blue, because the declaration written first is always prioritized
A mix of teal, because the browser combines both pigment values
Green, because the cascading rule gives precedence to the rule in the last position
Black, because a conflict between two color values causes the browser to cancel the style
questionPool.explanation: The cascading principle reads CSS from top to bottom. When there are two rules with the same specificity on the same element, the rule written lowest/last is applied.

questionPool.question: What is the function of adding '!important' to a CSS declaration (for example: 'color: red !important;')?
options: Marks that the property applies only in offline mode
Speeds up the browser's download of the CSS file
Turns the text bold and makes it blink
Forces that declaration to win and ignore the normal rule reading order
questionPool.explanation: !important gives a declaration the highest priority, overriding the normal cascading order. It should be used wisely because it makes debugging harder.

questionPool.question: What is the main difference between specifying colors using color names (color keywords) and hex codes in CSS?
options: Color names are only for inline styles, whereas hex codes are for external files
Hex codes provide millions of color variations, whereas color names have limited options
Color names are obsolete and no longer supported by modern browsers today
Hex codes can only be used for text color, not for backgrounds
questionPool.explanation: Color names (such as red, blue) are limited to a standard list of keywords, whereas hex codes (#RRGGBB) provide the flexibility to produce over 16 million color combinations.

questionPool.question: Which is an example of valid hex code syntax for the color property in CSS?
questionPool.explanation: Hexadecimal codes in CSS must start with a hash sign (#) followed by a combination of numbers and letters (for example #1E90FF).

questionPool.question: Which CSS property is specifically used to change the text color of an element?
questionPool.explanation: In the CSS standard, the property for coloring text is 'color', not 'font-color' or 'text-color'.

questionPool.question: Based on the CSS basics summary, which of the following statements is MOST ACCURATE?
options: CSS is a declarative language that controls visual presentation, where child elements can inherit their parent's styles
CSS rules are read randomly without paying attention to the order of lines of code
Inline style is the most recommended method for industry-standard web development
CSS is responsible for managing data flow logic and database storage
questionPool.explanation: CSS works specifically for declarative visual presentation, takes advantage of inheritance from parent elements, and is read in order according to cascading rules.

questionPool.question: After understanding CSS basics (syntax, selectors, and coloring), what topic is commonly learned at the next stage to arrange the layout of a web page?
options: SQL database connections and server queries
Box model, layout (such as flexbox/grid), and responsive design
questionPool.explanation: After mastering basic styling, the next step in CSS is learning the box model, layout (layout/positioning), and responsive design for different screen sizes.

questionPool.question: Which selector can be used across multiple elements of different types at once (shareable), unlike the id selector which must be unique?
questionPool.explanation: The class selector is shareable: a single class name can be applied to many elements, even across different tag types. An ID must be unique throughout the entire document.

questionPool.question: Consider the selector: img[alt]. Which elements will match this rule?
options: Only img elements with an empty alt value
Only img elements that have an alt attribute, regardless of its value
All img elements, regardless of their attributes
All elements that have any attribute
questionPool.explanation: The [attr] form in an attribute selector targets elements that possess that attribute, regardless of its value.

questionPool.question: What is the main difference between the adjacent sibling selector (+) and the general sibling selector (~)?
options: + only works on inline elements, ~ is for block elements
~ requires using a target class, whereas + only applies to tags
+ selects the single immediate next sibling, ~ selects all following siblings
Both behave identically for styling, only differing in symbol character
questionPool.explanation: The adjacent sibling selector (+) only matches the second element that immediately follows the first element. The general sibling selector (~) matches all occurrences of the second element that appear after it, as long as they share the same parent.

questionPool.question: The selector .kotak > p will only target paragraphs that...
options: Are located anywhere inside .kotak, no matter how deeply nested
questionPool.explanation: The child selector (>) only targets direct children, unlike the descendant selector (space) which reaches all descendants at any nesting depth.

questionPool.question: The property content: ""; must be specified for the following pseudo-elements to appear, except...
questionPool.explanation: :hover is a pseudo-class (selecting based on state), not a pseudo-element, so it does not require the content property. ::before and ::after must have content in order to render.

questionPool.question: Why is writing font-size: 1.5 em; (with a space) considered invalid by browsers?
options: Because the em unit is only allowed for margin, not for font size
Because decimal numbers must be rounded to the nearest whole number
Because CSS measurement values and units must be written together without a space
Because modern web browser engines only accept pixel (px) units
questionPool.explanation: Values and units on size properties such as font-size must be written directly adjacent without a space, for example 1.5em. If there is a space, the entire declaration is ignored by the browser.

questionPool.question: Which font-size unit is calculated relative to the font size of the root element (<html>), making it more predictable than em?
questionPool.explanation: rem is relative to the root element's font size, whereas em is relative to the font size of the element itself, which can compound when used repeatedly on nested elements.

questionPool.question: The shorthand font: italic bold 16px/1.5 sans-serif; follows the order...
questionPool.explanation: The font shorthand must follow the order style weight size/line-height family. If the order is wrong, the entire declaration is considered invalid.

questionPool.question: Which property is used to change text capitalization to all uppercase without modifying the original text in HTML?
questionPool.explanation: text-transform changes the visual capitalization (for example, uppercase) without altering the source text in HTML, keeping it friendly for search and screen readers.

questionPool.question: Which statement is true about color formats in CSS?
options: The HSL format only applies to background properties, not to text
HEX color codes must begin with an opening rgb( parenthesis
RGB uses numeric values from 0-255, whereas HEX notation is hexadecimal-based
Standard named colors support millions of color shades just like HEX values
questionPool.explanation: RGB specifies red, green, and blue values from 0-255 each. HEX is a compact six-digit hexadecimal representation of the same RGB combination.

questionPool.question: What happens if an element is given opacity: 0%?
options: The element along with all its contents becomes completely invisible
The element is displayed in solid black
The element remains visible, but its color turns gray
questionPool.explanation: opacity: 0% makes the element along with all its contents and descendants completely invisible, unlike an alpha channel which only makes a specific color transparent.

questionPool.question: A box has width: 200px, padding: 20px, and border: 2px solid. With box-sizing: content-box (default), what is the total width of the box?
questionPool.explanation: With content-box, padding and border are added outside of width: 200 + (20x2) + (2x2) = 244px. With border-box, the total width would remain 200px.

questionPool.question: The property box-sizing: border-box; is useful for...
options: Hiding an element's border lines without changing the physical size of the box
Making padding and border included within the specified element width
Removing all default margin spacing that HTML elements have
Rounding the corners of an element's border smoothly and symmetrically
questionPool.explanation: border-box keeps the final size of an element (including padding and border) matching the specified width, which is very useful when building layouts with floats or percentages.

questionPool.question: Two sibling elements are stacked vertically: the top element has margin-bottom: 30px, and the bottom element has margin-top: 20px. What is the final space between them?
options: 30px, because margin collapsing uses the larger value
50px, because both vertical margin values are added together by the browser
20px, because CSS rules prioritize the smallest margin value
0px, because both vertical margins cancel each other out
questionPool.explanation: Vertical margins between siblings undergo margin collapsing: their values are not added together, but instead the larger of the two is used.

questionPool.question: What is the main requirement for the margin: 0 auto; technique to successfully center an element horizontally?
options: The element must be given display: inline
The element must have padding larger than its margin
The element must have a specified width
The element must be inside an element with position: relative
questionPool.explanation: Without a specified width, a block element fills the full width of its parent, leaving no leftover horizontal space on the left and right for centering.

questionPool.question: Which display value prevents an element from starting a new line (like inline), while still allowing its dimensions to be set with width and height (like block)?
questionPool.explanation: inline-block combines two behaviors: it does not create a new line like inline, yet its dimensions can still be set like block.

questionPool.question: The properties top, left, right, and bottom only take effect if the element has a position value of...
options: They have no relation to position
questionPool.explanation: The top/right/bottom/left properties only work on elements outside normal static positioning, namely position relative, absolute, or fixed. On static (default), these properties have no effect.

questionPool.question: What is the main difference between position: relative and position: absolute regarding the space left behind by the element?
options: Both remove the element's allocated space from the normal document flow
absolute preserves the original allocated space, while relative removes it
relative preserves the element's original space, while absolute removes its space
Both preserve empty space at the element's original position in the document
questionPool.explanation: relative keeps space reserved at its original position as if the element were still there. absolute removes the element completely from the flow, so elements below it move up to fill that space.

questionPool.question: position: fixed is always calculated relative to...
options: The browser window, staying in place even when the page is scrolled
The mobile viewport size only; it does not apply on desktop
The nearest parent element, regardless of the parent's position
questionPool.explanation: Unlike absolute, which can be relative to a non-static positioned ancestor, fixed is always relative to the browser window and does not move when the page is scrolled.

questionPool.question:
A
contains only a single with float: left, and the div has no other styling. What happens to the height of that
?
options: The div element hits a rendering error and the image does not display at all
The element's height doubles compared to the original image dimensions
The element's height automatically expands to match the image inside it
Its height becomes 0px because the floated element leaves the parent's normal flow
questionPool.explanation: A floated element is taken out of normal flow, so the parent does not account for it when calculating height. This is the common parent collapse issue when using float.

questionPool.question: Two common ways to fix a parent element losing its height due to floated child elements are...
options: Applying a combination of display: none and opacity: 0 on the parent container
Using a closing clear property or overflow: auto on the parent element
Removing all floated elements from the parent container's structure
Replacing all float properties with a combination of negative margin and padding
questionPool.explanation: clear (usually on an empty element after the floated elements) and overflow: auto on the parent are two common techniques to make the parent calculate the height of its floated children again.

questionPool.question: What is the main function of the meta tag <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">?
options: Speeding up web page file downloads on slow mobile connections
Matching the browser's viewport width to the physical screen size of the device
Enabling automatic dark mode for all user interface components
Disabling external CSS file loading on mobile phone screens
questionPool.explanation: Without this meta tag, mobile browsers tend to display the page zoomed out to fit a small screen, making text too small to read.

options: An error occurs because the two rules conflict
Its width stays 25%, and the media query is ignored
The aside element disappears from the page
Its width becomes 100%, because the max-width: 600px condition is met
questionPool.explanation: Because 500px is smaller than the specified max-width: 600px limit, the rule inside the media query applies and overrides the previous rule, making aside 100% wide.

questionPool.question: position: sticky is a combination of the behaviors of two other position values, namely...
questionPool.explanation: sticky behaves like relative until it reaches a viewport edge, then sticks like fixed once it hits the specified offset (for example, top: 0) as the page is scrolled.

questionPool.question: What is the main benefit of minifying CSS files before using them on a production website?
options: Reducing file size so the page loads faster in the browser
Unlocking experimental CSS features that are not yet stable in browsers
Making the CSS code structure much neater for humans to read
Automatically increasing color brightness and contrast in the UI
questionPool.explanation: Minification removes whitespace, line breaks, and comments that do not affect CSS functionality, resulting in a smaller file size and faster page loads.

courses.title: Modern CSS Layout: Flexbox & Grid
courses.description: Master modern web layout techniques using one-dimensional CSS Flexbox and two-dimensional CSS Grid to build flexible, responsive, and professional web interfaces.
prerequisites: Selesai Fondasi Web: Dari Nol ke Baris Kode Pertama

quizQuestions.question: Which CSS Flexbox property is used to align and distribute items along the main axis?
quizQuestions.explanation: justify-content distributes remaining free space and controls item alignment along the main axis (horizontal by default when flex-direction: row).

quizQuestions.question: What does the display: grid property do on a CSS container element?
options: Enables a two-dimensional grid layout for rows and columns
Hides the element from visual rendering and browser accessibility
Removes all padding and margin from child elements inside it
Converts the element into plain inline text without box dimensions
quizQuestions.explanation: display: grid activates a two-dimensional grid layout system that allows positioning child elements simultaneously in rows and columns.

quizQuestions.question: What is the fundamental philosophical difference between CSS Flexbox and CSS Grid?
options: Flexbox only works in desktop browsers, whereas Grid works in all browsers
Flexbox only arranges text layout, whereas Grid arranges image layout
Flexbox requires JavaScript dependencies, whereas Grid is pure CSS
Flexbox is a 1-dimensional layout, whereas Grid is a 2-dimensional layout
quizQuestions.explanation: Flexbox is designed to arrange the flow of elements along a single linear dimension, while CSS Grid is designed to define a two-dimensional blueprint of rows and columns at once.

quizQuestions.question: Why was using the CSS float property to divide page columns considered problematic in the past?
options: Because older browsers refused to render colors on elements with the float property
Because float removes child elements from the page DOM document hierarchy
Because elements are taken out of normal flow, causing their parent to collapse
Because it triggers high CPU usage that slows down browser rendering
quizQuestions.explanation: Floated elements are lifted out of normal flow, causing the parent container's height to collapse to 0 (container collapsing) and requiring clearfix hacks.

quizQuestions.question: What behavior immediately happens to direct child elements when a parent element is given 'display: flex'?
options: Child elements are automatically converted in structure to HTML table elements
All text inside child elements is automatically formatted in italics
Child elements line up horizontally in a row and automatically match heights
All child elements are temporarily hidden from the browser display flow
quizQuestions.explanation: Enabling display: flex makes direct children line up horizontally (default row) and by default stretch to equalize their height along the cross axis.

quizQuestions.question: If a container has 'flex-direction: column', which direction does the Main Axis flow?
options: Diagonally from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner
Vertically downward from top to bottom
quizQuestions.explanation: With flex-direction: column, the main axis changes direction to vertical from top to bottom, while the cross axis becomes horizontal.

quizQuestions.question: Which justify-content value is most commonly used in a Navbar to place the logo on the far left and the menu on the far right?
quizQuestions.explanation: space-between places the first item at the start edge, the last item at the end edge, and distributes the remaining space evenly between them.

quizQuestions.question: Which two lines of CSS Flexbox declarations produce perfect centering (horizontally and vertically centered)?
quizQuestions.explanation: Combining justify-content: center (on the main axis) and align-items: center (on the cross axis) centers elements perfectly in both directions.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the 'flex-wrap: wrap' property on a Flexbox container?
options: Wraps all text inside the container in special parentheses
Turns the outer border of the container into a decorative folding frame
Allows elements to wrap onto a new line when the container width is insufficient
Prevents elements from overflowing by clipping content that exceeds the container bounds
quizQuestions.explanation: By default Flexbox uses nowrap (forcing a single line). flex-wrap: wrap allows child elements to move onto new lines when horizontal space runs out.

quizQuestions.question: What is the advantage of using the 'gap: 16px' property compared to adding margins to Flexbox/Grid child elements?
options: gap adds spacing between items without adding extra margins against the outer walls
gap turns the background color between elements transparent
gap dynamically calculates spacing proportions using screen percentages
gap can be applied automatically only to interactive image elements
quizQuestions.explanation: gap provides clean spacing strictly between child element cells without adding extra margin on the outer edges of the container.

quizQuestions.question: What does the shorthand declaration 'flex: 1' mean when applied to multiple Flexbox child elements?
options: All elements divide the remaining container space equally and uniformly
Only the first element in order is allowed to stretch to fill the container
Elements are prohibited from shrinking even when space inside the container runs out
All elements are forced to have a fixed size of exactly one pixel
quizQuestions.explanation: flex: 1 is shorthand for flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 1, flex-basis: 0%, which distributes remaining space equally among all items that have it.

quizQuestions.question: Does manipulating visual order using the 'order: -1' property change the reading order for Screen Readers and Tab key navigation?
options: Yes, the server-side HTML document is mutated to match the display order
No, order only changes visual appearance; the DOM accessibility order stays the same
Yes, the DOM reading order and Tab key navigation shift automatically as well
It depends on the web browser and the device type used by the user
quizQuestions.explanation: The order property only manipulates visual presentation on screen and does not alter the original HTML document structure (DOM order) for screen readers and keyboard navigation.

quizQuestions.question: What does the '1fr' unit mean in the declaration 'grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr'?
options: The full height of one row from the container downward
One fractional share of the remaining space after 200px
An animation speed of one frame per second in the browser
A relative size equivalent to one root em in the browser
quizQuestions.explanation: The fr (fractional unit) allocates a fraction of the remaining free space in the container after fixed widths (such as 200px) and gaps are accounted for.

quizQuestions.question: How do you concisely write 4 columns each 1fr wide using CSS Grid?
quizQuestions.explanation: The repeat(4, 1fr) function is the standard way to repeat a 1fr size declaration 4 times.

quizQuestions.question: Which CSS Grid declaration spans a card element from column grid line 1 to column grid line 3?
quizQuestions.explanation: grid-column: 1 / 3 (or grid-column: span 2) stretches an element starting from grid line 1 to grid line 3.

quizQuestions.question: What is the magic behind the pattern 'grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))'?
options: Rotates card content orientation by two hundred degrees in a circle
Creates an automatic responsive gallery without media queries across screen sizes
Removes card elements whose width is below a minimum limit of two hundred pixels
Restricts the card gallery layout to always consist of exactly one column
quizQuestions.explanation: The combination of auto-fit and minmax automatically calculates how many columns fit and wraps rows responsively without needing a single @media query.

questionPool.question: Which CSS property enables Flexbox mode on a container?
questionPool.explanation: display: flex; turns an element into a flex container and its direct children into flex items.

questionPool.question: If flex-direction is set to row, which direction does the Main Axis run?
questionPool.explanation: With flex-direction: row (default), the Main Axis runs horizontally and the Cross Axis runs vertically.

questionPool.question: Which property controls item alignment along the Main Axis in Flexbox?
questionPool.explanation: justify-content controls space distribution and alignment along the Main Axis.

questionPool.question: What declaration allows flex items to automatically wrap onto a new line when space is narrow?
questionPool.explanation: flex-wrap: wrap; allows items to wrap onto the next line instead of being forced to shrink.

questionPool.question: Which modern property adds spacing between Flexbox or Grid items without margin hacks?
questionPool.explanation: The gap property adds consistent spacing only between items, not on the outer edges.

questionPool.question: What is the main advantage of CSS Grid compared to Flexbox?
options: It handles 2-dimensional layouts (rows and columns simultaneously)
It does not require a modern browser
questionPool.explanation: CSS Grid is designed for 2-dimensional layouts (rows and columns together), while Flexbox excels at 1-dimensional layouts.

questionPool.question: What does the fr unit mean in grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr;?
options: Fraction of the remaining available free space
questionPool.explanation: 1fr and 2fr divide the container's remaining free space in a 1-to-2 ratio.

questionPool.question: Which CSS function creates an automatically responsive gallery column layout without media queries?
questionPool.explanation: The combination repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) automatically adjusts the number of columns based on the container width.

questionPool.question: Which CSS rule is used to apply styles only at specific screen widths?
questionPool.explanation: @media queries enable responsive breakpoints based on viewport size.

questionPool.question: Which CSS Grid property centers content both horizontally and vertically at once?
questionPool.explanation: place-items: center; is shorthand for align-items: center and justify-items: center.

courses.cheatSheetMarkdown:
# Modern CSS Layout Cheat Sheet

## Flexbox (1-Dimensional)
- `display: flex;` — Enable flex container
- `flex-direction: row | column;` — Main Axis direction
- `justify-content: flex-start | center | space-between | space-evenly;` — Main Axis alignment
- `align-items: stretch | center | flex-start | flex-end;` — Cross Axis alignment
- `flex-wrap: wrap;` — Allow items to wrap onto new lines
- `gap: 16px;` — Spacing between items

## CSS Grid (2-Dimensional)
- `display: grid;` — Enable grid container
- `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);` — 3 equal-width columns
- `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr));` — Auto-responsive gallery
- `place-items: center;` — Center vertically & horizontally

## Responsive
```css
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
}
```

quizQuestions.question: Which variable declaration keyword prevents its value from being reassigned?

The === operator checks both value and data type equality. Since a is a number and b is a string, the result is false.

options: On the first line of the document before <!DOCTYPE html>
quizQuestions.explanation: Placing the script tag right before the closing body tag ensures all HTML elements have been downloaded and parsed by the browser before the script runs.

quizQuestions.question: What standard JavaScript command is used to print information or values to the developer console?
quizQuestions.explanation: console.log() is the standard command for printing output to the developer console.

quizQuestions.question: What type of error appears when you reference a variable that has never been declared?
quizQuestions.explanation: A ReferenceError occurs when JavaScript tries to look up a variable name that cannot be found in memory/scope.

quizQuestions.question: What is the result of the expression typeof 'CodeAcademy'?
quizQuestions.explanation: The typeof operator returns the string 'string' for all text data enclosed in quotes.

quizQuestions.question: What is the result of the arithmetic operation 14 % 4?
quizQuestions.explanation: The modulo operator (%) produces the remainder of integer division. 14 divided by 4 equals 3 with a remainder of 2.

quizQuestions.question: What keyword must be included at the end of each case block in a switch statement so execution does not fall through to the case below it?
quizQuestions.explanation: The break statement stops evaluation of the switch block and exits it, preventing fall-through behavior.

quizQuestions.question: Which statement is TRUE regarding a variable declared with 'const' inside curly braces {}?
options: It can only be accessed within that curly-brace block (Block Scope)
It will produce a SyntaxError when the program runs
It can be accessed freely from outside the curly braces anywhere
It automatically becomes a global variable
quizQuestions.explanation: const and let variables have block scope, meaning they are isolated within the curly braces where they are declared.

quizQuestions.question: Given the object const pengguna = { nama: 'Rani', umur: 21 }, how do you read the umur property using dot notation?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dot notation uses a period between the object name and the property name: pengguna.umur.

quizQuestions.question: Which document method is used to select the first HTML element that has the id 'tombol-kirim'?
quizQuestions.explanation: document.querySelector() uses CSS selectors, where the hash symbol (#) indicates searching by an element's id.

quizQuestions.question: Which method is used to register a click handler function on an HTML button element?
quizQuestions.explanation: addEventListener('click', handler) is the standard method for handling click events on DOM elements.

quizQuestions.question: Which keyword is paired with 'async' inside a function to wait for a Promise to settle in a non-blocking manner?
quizQuestions.explanation: The await keyword can only be used inside a function prefixed with the async keyword.

quizQuestions.question: Which array method is used to add a new item to the very end of an array?
quizQuestions.explanation: The .push() method inserts one or more new elements at the end of an array and updates its length.

sectionQuizzes.title: JS Logic & Data Structures Core Quiz

questionPool.question: Which keyword should be prioritized when declaring a variable whose value will not be reassigned?
questionPool.explanation: Use const by default to keep variable references safe from accidental changes; use let only when the value needs to change.

questionPool.question: Which comparison operator checks equality of both value and data type?
questionPool.explanation: === (strict equality) compares both value and data type without implicit type conversion.

questionPool.question: Which array method adds a new element to the end of an array?
questionPool.explanation: .push() adds one or more elements to the end of an array.

questionPool.question: How do you access the nama property from the object const user = { nama: 'Rani' };?
questionPool.explanation: In JavaScript, object properties are accessed using dot notation (user.nama) or bracket notation (user['nama']).

questionPool.question: Which is a valid Arrow Function syntax in ES6?
questionPool.explanation: Arrow functions use the syntax (parameters) => expression or block { ... }.

questionPool.question: Which DOM method selects the first element that matches a CSS selector?
questionPool.explanation: document.querySelector('#id' or '.class') returns the first element that matches the CSS selector.

questionPool.question: Which property is safer to use for changing an element's text content without executing HTML?
questionPool.explanation: textContent inserts plain text, making it safer against XSS risks compared to innerHTML.

questionPool.question: Which method is used to attach a button click handler to a DOM element?
questionPool.explanation: addEventListener('click', fn) is the modern DOM standard for handling events.

questionPool.question: Why is event.preventDefault() often called on a form submit event?
options: To prevent the page from automatically reloading when the form is submitted
questionPool.explanation: event.preventDefault() stops the form's default behavior so we can process the data via JavaScript without reloading.

questionPool.question: Which array method produces a new array containing elements that pass a specific condition?
questionPool.explanation: .filter() returns a new array containing elements for which the callback returns true.
